title: Reflected and Stored XSS with a real lab
description: Inject real JavaScript into a vulnerable app: reflected XSS, stored XSS and payload bypass.

1.title: Reflected XSS: your code in the response
1.body:
## Reflected: the input comes back unwashed Start the lab and try: ```bash # Normal curl "http://127.0.0.1:18082/hello?name=Ana" # Response:

Hello, Ana!

# XSS: your input IS HTML/JS code curl "http://127.0.0.1:18082/hello?name=" # Response:

Hello, !

``` The browser receives YOUR `` 2. The victim clicks → the browser runs your script 3. Your script sends the victim's session cookies to your server 4. With the cookie, you impersonate the victim The mitigation: `html.escape()` in Python, `textContent` in JavaScript, CSP headers. ## Retrieve the lab flag The lab has a flag hidden in the /search endpoint. When you search for the word "XSS", the response contains the flag: ```bash curl "http://127.0.0.1:18082/search?q=XSS" ``` Look for the flag in the response body.

xss-reflejado-t01-q01.prompt: What HTML tag executes JavaScript in the browser?

xss-reflejado-t01-q02.prompt: What Python function SANITIZES HTML (and is deliberately NOT used by this lab)?

xss-reflejado-t01-q03.prompt: Search for 'XSS' in the lab's /search endpoint. Submit the flag.

2.title: Stored XSS: the poison that persists
2.body: ## Stored XSS: poison once, affect everyone The lab has a **guestbook** (`/guestbook`). xss-reflejado-t02-q01.prompt: Which type of XSS is MORE dangerous: reflected or stored?
xss-reflejado-t02-q01.hint: Stored XSS stays saved and affects everyone who views the page.

options.b: Stored: it runs automatically for EVERY visitor, no click needed

xss-reflejado-t02-q02.prompt: What JavaScript property (the one that gives access to the page's cookies) is the classic target of an XSS payload?
